translation_en: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me—the wording is his—saying: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: I heard Suwayd ibn Ghafalah say: Zayd ibn Suhan, Salman ibn Rabi'ah, and I went out on an expedition and found a whip. I picked it up, but they told me to leave it. I said I would announce it; if its owner came, I would return it, otherwise I would make use of it. I would not agree with them. When we returned, I was destined to make pilgrimage and came to Madinah. I met Ubayy ibn Ka'b and told him about the whip and what the two men had said. He said: In the Messenger of Allah's time I found a purse containing one hundred dinars. I brought it to the Messenger of Allah, who said: Announce it for a year. I did so but found no one who recognized it. I returned to him, and he again said to announce it for a year. I did so and found no claimant. I returned again, and he again said to announce it for a year. I did so and found no claimant. He said: Remember its amount, container, and tie. If its owner comes, return it; otherwise, make use of it. So I used it. Later I met him in Makkah, and he said: I do not know whether he said three years or one year.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr al-'Abdi narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed me—or informed the people while I was among them—saying: I heard Suwayd ibn Ghafalah say: I went out with Zayd ibn Suhan and Salman ibn Rabi'ah and found a whip. He related the hadith similarly up to the words, So I used it. Shu'bah said: I heard him ten years later say: He announced it for one year.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us. Another chain: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us, all from Sufyan. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah, Ibn 'Amr, narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah. Another chain: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to us: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us. All of them reported from Salamah ibn Kuhayl with this chain, like Shu'bah's hadith. All of their reports mention three years, except Hammad ibn Salamah's, which says two or three years. The reports of Sufyan, Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, and Hammad say: If someone comes and tells you its amount, container, and tie, give it to him. Sufyan's version through Waki' adds: Otherwise it is like your own property; Ibn Numayr's says: Otherwise make use of it.

Abu al-Tahir and Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Ashajj, from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Taymi: The Messenger of Allah forbade taking found property belonging to pilgrims.

Abu al-Tahir and Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bakr ibn Sawadah, from Abu Salim al-Jayshani, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: Whoever shelters a lost animal is himself lost, unless he announces it.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi said: I read to Malik ibn Anas, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: No one should milk another person's livestock without permission. Would any of you like someone to come to his drinking place, break open his store-room, and carry away his food? Their livestock's udders are their food stores, so no one should milk another person's livestock without permission.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Rumh both reported from al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us. Another chain: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us, both from 'Ubaydullah. Another chain: Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us. Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma'il, Ibn 'Ulayyah, narrated to us. All reported from Ayyub. Another chain: Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub; and Ibn Jurayj from Musa. All reported from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, with the like of Malik's hadith. All their reports say the food is taken out, except al-Layth ibn Sa'd's report, which says it is carried away, like Malik's wording.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: We asked, Messenger of Allah, you send us out and we stay with people who do not host us. What do you think? The Messenger of Allah said: If you stay with a people and they provide what is appropriate for a guest, accept it. If they do not, take from them the guest's due that is appropriate for them.

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Abu al-Ashhab narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: While we were traveling with the Prophet, a man came riding his mount and began looking right and left. The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever has an extra mount should give it to someone without a mount, and whoever has extra provisions should give them to someone without provisions. He mentioned the different kinds of property until we thought that none of us had any right to keep surplus.

Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to me: al-Nadr, Ibn Muhammad al-Yamami, narrated to us: 'Ikrimah, Ibn 'Ammar, narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to us, from his father, who said: We went with the Messenger of Allah on an expedition and suffered such hardship that we considered slaughtering some of our riding animals. The Prophet ordered us to gather our food bags. We spread out a leather mat and the people's provisions were gathered on it. I looked to estimate its size; it seemed like a goat lying down, while we were fourteen hundred. We all ate until satisfied, then filled our bags. The Prophet asked if there was water for ablution. A man brought a small water-skin with only a little water in it and poured it into a cup. We all performed ablution, each pouring water generously; we were fourteen hundred. Afterward eight men came and asked for water for purification. The Messenger of Allah said: The water for ablution has run out.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Sulaym ibn Akhdar narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, who said: I wrote to Nafi' asking him about calling before fighting. He wrote back: That was only in the early days of Islam. The Messenger of Allah raided Banu al-Mustaliq while they were unaware and their livestock were being watered. He killed their fighters and took their families captive. That day he captured—Yahya said, I think he said—Juwayriyah, or he definitely said—the daughter of al-Harith. 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who was in that army, also related this to me.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, with this chain and the like of it. He said Juwayriyah daughter of al-Harith, without expressing uncertainty.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Sufyan. Another chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Sufyan dictated it to us. Another chain: 'Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to me—the wording is his—'Abd al-Rahman, Ibn Mahdi, narrated to me: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah appointed a commander over an army or detachment, he advised him personally to fear Allah and to treat the Muslims with him well. Then he said: Go out in Allah's name and in Allah's cause. Fight those who disbelieve in Allah. Do not steal from the spoils, betray, mutilate, or kill a child. When you meet your polytheist enemy, invite them to three alternatives—or three matters—and accept whichever they agree to, then leave them alone. Invite them to Islam; if they accept, accept that from them and leave them alone. Then invite them to move from their land to the land of the emigrants, and tell them that if they do so they will have the emigrants' rights and obligations. If they refuse to move, tell them they will be like the Muslim Bedouins, subject to Allah's rule that applies to believers, but they will have no share of the spoils or public revenue unless they fight alongside the Muslims. If they refuse, ask them to pay the jizyah. If they agree, accept it and leave them alone; if they refuse, seek Allah's help and fight them. If you besiege a fortress and they ask you to grant them Allah's covenant and the covenant of His Prophet, do not grant them Allah's or His Prophet's covenant, but grant them your covenant and that of your companions. It is less serious for you to violate your own covenant and that of your companions than to violate Allah's covenant and His Messenger's. If you besiege a fortress and they ask to surrender under Allah's judgment, do not make them surrender under Allah's judgment; make them surrender under your judgment, for you do not know whether you will reach Allah's judgment concerning them. 'Abd al-Rahman said: This or something like it. Ishaq added at the end of his report from Yahya ibn Adam: I related this hadith to Muqatil ibn Hayyan—Yahya said, meaning that 'Alqamah was saying it to Ibn Hayyan—and he said: Muslim ibn Haysam narrated to me, from al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin, from the Prophet, something similar.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to me: Shu'bah narrated to us: 'Alqamah ibn Marthad narrated to me that Sulayman ibn Buraydah told him, from his father, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah sent out a commander or detachment, he would call him and advise him. He related the hadith with the meaning of Sufyan's report.
Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Farra' narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn al-Walid, from Shu'bah, with this report.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us. The wording is Abu Bakr's. They said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah sent one of his companions on an errand, he would say: Give good news and do not drive people away; make things easy and do not make them difficult.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, from his grandfather: The Prophet sent him and Mu'adh to Yemen and said: Make things easy, do not make them difficult; give good news, do not drive people away; cooperate and do not disagree.

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr. Another chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi Khalaf reported from Zakariyya ibn 'Adi: 'Ubaydullah informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah. Both reported from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet, with the like of Shu'bah's hadith. Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah's report does not include cooperate and do not disagree.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: I came to the Prophet with two men from my cousins. One said, Messenger of Allah, appoint us over some of what Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has entrusted to you. The other said the same. He replied: By Allah, we do not appoint to this work anyone who asks for it or is eager for it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us; the wording is Ibn Hatim's. They said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us: Abu Burdah narrated to me. Abu Musa said: I came to the Prophet with two men from the Ash'ari tribe, one on my right and one on my left. Both asked for a position, while the Prophet was using a tooth-stick. He said: What do you say, Abu Musa—or 'Abdullah ibn Qays? I said: By the One who sent you with the truth, they did not tell me what was in their hearts, and I did not know they were seeking office. I could almost see the tooth-stick beneath his lip as it withdrew. He said: We do not appoint to our work anyone who seeks it. But go, Abu Musa—or 'Abdullah ibn Qays. He sent him to Yemen, then sent Mu'adh ibn Jabal after him. When Mu'adh arrived, Abu Musa said, Come down, and laid out a cushion for him. A man was there bound. Mu'adh asked what it was. Abu Musa said: He was a Jew, became Muslim, then returned to his bad religion and became a Jew again. Mu'adh said: I will not sit until he is killed according to Allah's and His Messenger's judgment. Abu Musa told him to sit, but Mu'adh repeated this three times. The man was then executed. They discussed night prayer. One of them, Mu'adh, said: As for me, I sleep and then rise, and I hope for the same reward in my sleep as I hope for when I stand in prayer.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. The wording is Qutaybah's. They said: Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet sent me and Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen. I said: Messenger of Allah, in our land a drink called mizr is made from barley, and a drink called bit' is made from honey. He said: Every intoxicant is forbidden.

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, who heard it from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, from his grandfather: The Prophet sent him and Mu'adh to Yemen and said: Give good news, make things easy, teach, and do not drive people away. I think he also said: Cooperate. When he turned to leave, Abu Musa returned and said: Messenger of Allah, they have a honey drink that is boiled until it thickens, and mizr made from barley. The Messenger of Allah said: Everything that intoxicates and turns one away from prayer is forbidden.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us. The wording is Ibn Abi Khalaf's. They said: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah, Ibn 'Amr, narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah. Abu Burdah narrated to us, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah sent me and Mu'adh to Yemen and said: Invite the people, give good news, do not drive them away, make things easy, and do not make things difficult. I said: Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling about two drinks we make in Yemen: bit', made from honey and left to ferment until strong, and mizr, made from corn and barley and left to ferment until strong. The Messenger of Allah had been given concise, comprehensive speech, and said: I forbid every intoxicant that intoxicates and turns one away from prayer.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. Both reported from Shu'bah, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say that the Messenger of Allah said: Make things easy and do not make them difficult; bring calm and do not drive people away.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr and Abu Usamah narrated to us. Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id, Abu Qudamah al-Sarakhsi, narrated to me: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us. All reported from 'Ubaydullah. Another chain: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—the wording is his—my father narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: On the Day of Resurrection, when Allah gathers the first and last peoples, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person, and it will be said: This is the betrayal of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us. Another chain: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: 'Affan narrated to us: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us. Both reported from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, with this hadith.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, who heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say that the Messenger of Allah said: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will raise a banner for the treacherous person, and it will be said: Is this not the betrayal of so-and-so?

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah and Salim, the two sons of 'Abdullah, that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us. Another chain: Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad, Ibn Ja'far, informed us. Both reported from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet, who said: Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: This is the betrayal of so-and-so.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us. Another chain: 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us. Both reported from Shu'bah with this chain. 'Abd al-Rahman's report does not include the words: It will be said, This is the betrayal of so-and-so.
